questions.prompt: What makes Amcache uniquely valuable among Windows execution-adjacent artifacts?
options: It records the exact execution time to the millisecond
It stores a SHA-1 hash of the file, which survives deletion of the binary and enables threat-intelligence pivoting
It cannot be deleted by an attacker
It records every command-line argument used
questions.explanation: No other standard Windows artifact in this cluster stores a file hash, which is what makes Amcache the pivot point when the binary itself is gone.

questions.prompt: Why does an Amcache entry not by itself establish that a file executed?
options: Amcache is written by the Microsoft Compatibility Appraiser as an inventory of files present on the system, which can include files that never ran
Amcache only records files that failed to execute
Execution data is stored in a separate hive
questions.explanation: The appraiser inventories binaries it finds. Presence and identity are established; execution is not, which is why Prefetch is read alongside it.

questions.prompt: A binary ran ten minutes ago and appears in Prefetch but not Amcache. What is the most likely explanation?
options: The Prefetch entry is a false positive
Amcache is populated by a scheduled task, so there is a normal timing lag before recently-run binaries are inventoried
Amcache has been deleted by the attacker
The binary was never actually executed
questions.explanation: Because a scheduled task drives Amcache population, recent execution can legitimately appear in Prefetch before Amcache catches up -- expected behavior rather than a contradiction.

questions.prompt: Why should Amcache.hve be copied along with its .LOG1 and .LOG2 transaction logs?
options: The logs contain the parsing key
The transaction logs may contain entries not yet flushed into the hive itself
The hive is unreadable without them
The logs contain the file hashes while the hive contains only paths
questions.explanation: Registry transaction logs can hold recent changes not yet written to the hive, so collecting only the .hve risks missing the most recent entries.
